root_cause_label: Incorrect Binary Heuristic (Misinterpretation of SQLite B-Tree Cell Value Encoding)
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent adopted a wrong heuristic at step 9 — treating the first byte after the testword string as the integer value — instead of properly decoding SQLite B-tree varint cell headers and IEEE-754 encoded doubles, producing an incorrect recover.json with wrong values for most entries and missing testword00.
t_err_evidence: heuristic extracts first nearby byte as value, misreading IEEE-754 doubles (e.g. testword09: 63, testword08: 64)
t_commit_evidence: After step 9 the agent never revises its parsing approach: steps 10-14 all build on the same flawed byte-scanning logic, and step 15 writes the incorrect JSON to disk. The flawed heuristic locks in the wrong result from step 9 onward.
t_surface_evidence: recover.json written with wrong values: testword05:15, testword08:64, testword09:63
trigger_explanation: The agent lacks knowledge of how SQLite encodes cell payloads: each cell uses a varint header followed by type-coded data (e.g., 0x01 for 1-byte int, 0x07 for IEEE-754 big-endian double). Without this knowledge, the agent invents an ad-hoc heuristic (first non-null nearby byte) that misreads IEEE-754 doubles as their leading byte (0x3f=63 instead of ~0.5, 0x40=64 instead of ~99.99) and misidentifies B-tree structure bytes as values.
